DIFFUSION MODELS 
APPENDIX J
The basic diffusion equation used to determine the downwind, ground level concentrations of effluents emitted from the proposed stacks is given by Equation 5.1 (Turner, 1970);
\chi = \frac{Q}{\pi \sigma_{y} \sigma_{z} \overline{U}} \exp \{-1/2 (H/\sigma_{z})^{2} \} \exp \{-1/2 (y/\sigma_{y})^{2} \}
 5.1
where:
\chi
 = concentration in micrograms per cubic meter (
\mu g/m^3
) at the point x,y,o from an elevated source with effective height, H.
Q = emission rate in micrograms per second
y = the standard deviation in the crosswind direction of the plume concentration distribution in meters
σ<sub>z</sub> = the standard deviation in the vertical of the plume concentration distribution in meters
U = mean wind speed in meters per second
H = effective height of emission in meters
x = distance downwind in the direction of the mean wind in meters
y = crosswind distance in meters
This equation assumes that the distribution of effluents downwind from a stack will be Gaussian (normal) in both the horizontal and vertical planes of the plume.
